name: Botros methenamine–trimethoprim trial
question: Does daily methenamine hippurate prevent culture-proven recurrent urinary tract infection as effectively as trimethoprim in adult women?

design.population: Ninety-two women older than 18 years with at least two culture-positive urinary tract infections in six months or three in one year were randomized.

verdictNote: No recurrence difference was detected; the abstract gives no noninferiority margin.
takeaway: In a randomized open-label trial of 92 women with recurrent UTI, daily methenamine hippurate and trimethoprim had the same observed 12-month culture-proven recurrence proportion in the reported intention-to-treat analysis (28/43 [65%] in each arm; P=1.00).

reports.label: 12-month randomized report
reports.citation: Botros C, Lozo S, Iyer S, et al. "Methenamine hippurate compared with trimethoprim for the prevention of recurrent urinary tract infections: a randomized clinical trial." *Int Urogynecol J.* 2022;33(3):571-580. doi:10.1007/s00192-021-04849-0
reports.followUp: Culture-proven UTI recurrence by 12 months after prophylaxis initiation; treatment for at least six months

results.measure: Participants with recurrence by 12 months, reported intention-to-treat analysis
results.note: The abstract reports no between-group difference but gives no prespecified noninferiority margin or confidence interval; 86 of 92 randomized women appear in this analysis.

results.measure: Participants with recurrence by 12 months, per-protocol analysis
results.note: The abstract states that per-protocol analysis addressed receipt of the alternative drug after randomization.

delivery.label: Prophylaxis duration
delivery.value: Daily methenamine hippurate or trimethoprim for a minimum of six months.
